source_text: X. Ἐπιμένοντος δὲ πάλιν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγοντος· Ὄμοσον τὴν Καίσαρος τύχην, ἀπεκρίνατο· Εἰ κενοδοξεῖς ἵνα ὀμόσω τὴν Καίσαρος τύχην, ὡς σὺ λέγεις, προσποιῇ δὲ ἀγνοεῖν με τίς εἰμι, μετὰ παρρησίας ἄκουε· Χριστιανός εἰμι. Εἰ δὲ θέλεις τὸν τοῦ Χριστιανισμοῦ μαθεῖν λόγον, δὸς ἡμέραν καὶ ἄκουσον. Ἔφη ὁ ἀνθύπατος· Πεῖσον τὸν δῆμον. Ὁ δὲ Πολύκαρπος εἶπεν· Σὲ μὲν κἂν λόγου ἠξίωσα· δεδιδάγμεθα γὰρ ἀρχαῖς καὶ ἐξουσίαις ὑπὸ θεοῦ τεταγμέναις τιμὴν κατὰ τὸ προσῆκον τὴν μὴ βλάπτουσαν ἡμᾶς ἀπονέμειν· ἐκείνους δὲ οὐχ ἡγοῦμαι ἀξίους τοῦ ἀπολογεῖσθαι αὐτοῖς.
pass_a_gloss: But as he persisted again and kept saying, Swear by Caesar's fortune, he answered: If you hold the empty opinion that I will swear by Caesar's fortune, as you say, and pretend you do not know who I am, hear with frank speech: I am a Christian. If you desire to learn the account of Christianity, grant a day and listen. The proconsul said: Persuade the crowd. And Polycarp said: You I have deemed worthy of reasoned discussion; for we have been taught to render to rulers and authorities appointed by God the fitting honor that does not injure us; but those men I do not deem worthy for me to make a defense to them.
pass_b_english: When he persisted once more and demanded, Swear by the fortune of Caesar, he answered: If you vainly suppose that I will swear by the fortune of Caesar, as you put it, while pretending not to know who I am, then hear it openly: I am a Christian. If you wish to learn the teaching of Christianity, appoint a day and listen.

The proconsul said, Persuade the crowd. But Polycarp said: You I have judged worthy of reasoned speech, for we are taught to render the fitting honor that does us no harm to rulers and authorities ordained by God (Romans 13:1; Romans 13:7), but I do not judge those others worthy to receive my defense.

research.sense_relied_on: reason for the ruler, none for the mob
